.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures are expected
through early next week.

The pattern will remain relatively stagnant through tomorrow, 
with a Nor'easter continuing to circulate off the Mid- Atlantic 
coast and high pressure gradually building to our north. 
Northerly winds will continue to advect dry air into the region,
leading to clear skies. Temperatures will be near seasonal 
normals, with highs in the 60s to near 70 and lows in the mid to
upper 30s (west of the Blue Ridge) to lower to middle 40s (east
of the Blue Ridge).

By Thursday, what remains of the upper reflection of the offshore 
closed low gradually becomes absorbed into a deep trough over 
eastern Canada. These adjoining features are slated to pull eastward 
into the Canadian Maritimes while upstream heights build across the 
Mississippi Valley. From Friday and into this weekend, this broad 
ridge axis advances eastward ahead of a trough inhabiting the 
western/central U.S. As this occurs, there are some hints of another 
upper low center getting pinched off near the Carolina coast. 
However, its far southward displacement should minimize any direct 
impacts from this system. Overall synoptic uncertainty does increase 
markedly toward the end of the weekend and into early next week. 
Most notably, it revolves around a split in the jet streams over the 
middle of the continent. 

Looking down at the surface, high pressure dominates through late 
week while becoming more centered over the northeastern U.S. by 
Saturday. This ensures continued tranquil weather heading toward the 
last week of October. Expect dry conditions along with abundant 
sunshine each day. The air mass will remain quite dry owing to the 
prevailing northerly component to the local wind fields. Most days 
should yield highs in the 60s (50s for the mountains). The coldest 
overnight periods will likely be Friday and Saturday nights as lows 
fall into the 30s to low 40s. With the growing season having ended 
from the Blue Ridge westward, it remains to be seen if any 
frost/freeze threats emerge off to the east.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions and northerly winds are expected through tomorrow.
A few gusts to around 15-20 knots may be possible at times at 
MTN, BWI, DCA, and IAD.

VFR conditions are anticipated for Thursday through Saturday given 
robust high pressure over the region. Winds through Friday will 
mainly be northerly with afternoon gusts to around 15 to 20 knots. 
As high pressure settles overhead, winds turn lighter by
Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
Persistent northerly flow is expected to continue over the
waters through Thursday as a Nor'easter continues to circulate
offshore and high pressure gradually builds to our north. Small
Craft Advisories remain in effect for the Lower Tidal Potomac
and Chesapeake Bay through the day Wednesday.

Expect a northerly wind to largely dominate through Friday before 
turning more northeasterly by the night. Small Craft Advisories may 
be needed on Thursday, but particularly by late Thursday into Friday 
morning given a northerly surge in the winds.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A Nor'easter will continue to circulate offshore through
Thursday as high pressure builds to our north. This will lead to
persistent northerly flow over the waters. Minor flooding may be
possible at many tidal sites tonight through the day Thursday, 
but some uncertainty still remains.
